title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on order-6 classes with a sigma walk, all arithmetic in instructions

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the order-6 classes {±1, ±λ, ±λ²} with 2^32 walks and 2^16 adders, using batched affine additions. Walks run in trails from fresh coins. Each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once with its coins, including a distinguished point first reached during a look-ahead. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails, so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D). A fruitless cycle escapes to twice the canonical point of its least-key member, a doubling with no table. A repeated class within a trail is one of three kinds, as in the good event of proof.md: a formal repeat of length at most 64, detected and escaped within the per-entry step bound (Lemmas E1 and E2); a formal repeat of length 65 or more, which the good event excludes and whose probability is in DELTA_CUT; or an accidental equality of formally distinct points, bounded by DELTA_LOOP, which includes re-entry into an escaped cycle (D2). Escape depth is controlled by DELTA_DEPTH (section 2.3) and by the exact certificate of section 2.4, that no k below 2^50 has 2^k in Gamma. Abandonment is bounded in Lemma T'' (section 5). The 2-cycle excess is an exact forced-return identity (Lemma FR, section 4). Its orientation premise L-ori, that the non-equal share is 1/6, is measured at A = 8, 64, 256 and 1024 (evidence/sign-law.json, evidence/sign_law.py) and not derived at production size. Total computation is at most 2^126.479214 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. Each walk step pays 821 instructions on the common path and a Markov reserve of 7.89 for rare work, that is 828.89 instructions per walk step at C=1000. Rare work is charged at forced-path maxima from a bounding build, and the meter aborts with probability at most 1/64 (counted in delta). Peak memory is at most 2^75.749960 bytes. Preprocessing, 2^47.131242 units, is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target. The success bound 0.395898 is the model bound 0.411524, less 1/64 for the meter, less DELTA_CUT (at most 3.3e-12, of which DELTA_LONG is the closure bound of section 3 under q = 1/6, and 4.9e-10 at the sensitivity value q = 0.18), less DELTA_ABANDON (1.5e-17), less 2^-20 for the other terms. The probability is over the uniform target x and the algorithm's coins. It relies on the disclosed premises in proof.md: H1, the random-mapping model for r-adding class walks, used only for the collision statistics; M1, the equivariant random-orientation model (a per-class uniform key, canonical coordinate fractions and orientation), with the orientation law L-ori; and H3, the representativeness of the measured common-path instruction counts. The table and every trail's coins are drawn from the operating system's randomness, which is a property of the specification and not a heuristic. The toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and the small-build formal test support these premises; they do not prove them. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (b=7) or y^2=x^3+4 subgroups (b=4) at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: fresh-coin trails with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images, index, both cycle rules and the escape to twice the canonical least-key point; each trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or at the cap. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails with a different anchor schedule (Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. Filters compare keys masked to filter_bits, and the distinguished-point test precedes every escape and look-ahead step. With check_all_replays every recorded trail is replayed, and any replay that misses its record is counted. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only.

Check Lemma 1 of proof.md on random and edge-case reduced values: the 64-bit fraction approximations g_0 = a_3 and g_1 (4x64-bit limbs) are within [0,1] and [0,8] of floor(2^64*(beta^j x mod p)/p), and the kernel's rule for the canonical rotation either agrees with the exact minimum or falls back to the exact computation.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic.
